findings.reason: a control that cannot fail makes case (2)'s proof vacuous at dispatch, and the only implementation that makes it fail (treat a directory absent from the record as unchanged) contradicts the section's own trust rule and would silently mask a moved directory.
findings.text: §15's case (2) controls the "an HTML file added to a moved directory is covered" arm by "drop the moved directory from the record, and the file is missing", but the deliverable trusts the record "only when it was written by a pass that stat-ed every recorded directory": a record whose entry for that directory has been dropped fails that test, so the read falls back to stat-ing every recorded directory, sees the move, scans the directory, and finds the file — the case's own assertion still holds and the control reddens nothing

findings.reason: the staleness is bounded by the detector's fast pass (10 s default, `reckon/change_streams.py:184`), which stats every recorded directory and fires on the move, so the served page corrects itself; the plan would be clearer stating that bound, but its measure and its path do not change.
findings.text: §15 requires "the tree's change generation is still the one that pass wrote" and names the kernel project watch as a generation source, but the kernel watch's events are consumed and relayed only by an open stream's handler (`reckon/serve.py:2805`, the sole `_invalidate_tree_views` caller outside the detector and its own definition), so with no stream open a local write advances no generation and the next `/_index` read — the read a page makes before it opens a stream — serves the pre-write file set, where the read it replaces would have scanned the moved directory and served the new document

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's case (2) control ("drop the moved directory from the record, and the file is missing") cannot redden the case it guards, because the section's own trust rule discards a record that does not cover every recorded directory.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §15 names the kernel project watch as one of the three sources that start a change generation, but the kernel watch never invalidates anything itself; its report reaches `_invalidate_tree_views` only through an open change stream's handler, so a local write with no stream open starts no generation and the record stays trusted across it.
